title: Bind the release handoff to the journal EVENT, not the journal stream, so a later append cannot read as tamper
description:
FILED BY THE GOVERNOR from a disclosure worker-7ac56b35 found WHILE DRILLING task-af9454f4 (disclosure (iv), msg-bda31040, 11:18Z). Filed rather than left in chat because it is a correctness defect in code that is landing now, and a chat message is not an owner.

=== THE DEFECT ===
A standing release-handoff binding refuses on read with `DIGEST_MISMATCH` as soon as its attempt journals AGAIN.

`handoff.ref` names the journal STREAM. A stream's digest legitimately moves every time an entry is appended. The reader recomputes the digest and compares, so it cannot distinguish "a later, legitimate append" from "someone tampered with the bytes" — the two are the same observation. The binding was correct when written and reads as corrupt afterwards, through no fault of any writer.

=== WHY task-af9454f4 DID NOT FIX IT, and why that was right ===
That row's DoD 3 REQUIRES the recomputation. The worker implemented it as specified, found this consequence while drilling, and PINNED IT WITH AN ARM rather than quietly weakening the check or silently shipping a known break. That is the correct handling: the row's DoD governs, and a documented consequence with a test beats an undocumented deviation. Do not treat the existing arm as a bug — it is the disclosure, and it is what will red when this row fixes the cause.

=== THE DURABLE FIX, as the discloser scoped it ===
Bind the journal EVENT rather than the stream: an (aggregate, sequence) pair identifies one immutable append, whose digest cannot move. A later append then changes the stream without touching the bound event, so a legitimate append stops presenting as tamper while a real tamper still does.

That needs a reader capability af9454f4 does not own — reading a specific journal event by aggregate + sequence and recomputing over THAT event's bytes. Measure whether such a reader exists before assuming it must be built; this board has broken four dependency links this week by finding a landed reader where a row assumed a missing one.

=== WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN ===
Do not fix this by removing or weakening the recomputation. A binding that stops verifying its own referent trades a false-positive tamper for a silent one, which is strictly worse and would satisfy a naive reading of this description. The recomputation stays; only its REFERENT changes from a moving stream to a fixed event.

=== SEQUENCING ===
Parked in BACKLOG behind task-af9454f4 (currently in REVIEW at commit d954894). Promote when that row is DONE — this row edits the module it delivers, and racing its QA would collide. Read `comment-c390921b` (the consumer contract) and `comment-f4324dcc` (the governor's forced-deviation ratification) on that row before planning.
definitionOfDone: The binding names an immutable referent. The stored handoff ref identifies ONE journal event by (aggregate, sequence) — or an equivalently immutable coordinate the plan names and justifies — rather than the journal stream. State in an inline contract why the chosen coordinate cannot move under a later append.

A LATER APPEND NO LONGER READS AS TAMPER. An arm appends to the journal AFTER the binding is written, then reads the binding: it verifies and does NOT refuse. This arm must be RED before the change on the pre-change reader, and its redness must be for `DIGEST_MISMATCH` specifically — the exact code the disclosure names — not merely for some refusal.

A REAL TAMPER STILL REFUSES. A second arm mutates the bound event's own bytes and still gets `DIGEST_MISMATCH` (or the successor code the plan names, stated explicitly). This is the anti-relaxation arm: a fix that stops verifying satisfies item 2 and fails here. Both arms exist, both are pinned by exact code AND layer.

The recomputation survives. `git grep` shows the reader still re-derives and compares a digest — no flag, no tolerance window, no skip path, no comparison that a caller can influence. Only the REFERENT changed.

task-af9454f4's disclosure arm is re-graded, not deleted. That row pinned the defective behaviour deliberately; this row flips its expectation and records the flip as a deliberate re-grade citing this row, in the recorded form used by task-93e8aab3. The subject survives; only the expected outcome changes.

Gates green and attributed, each command's own exit code echoed: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Foreign dirty paths recorded and attributed by path if the shared tree is hot; a failing set that MOVES between two runs while your diff holds is a live peer, not a regression.
taskRails: STEP 1 IS VERIFY-OR-BLOCK. At YOUR head, from the COMMIT not the worktree: (a) confirm the reader still recomputes over a stream-derived ref; (b) `git grep` for an existing reader that fetches a journal event by aggregate + sequence — if one exists this row COMPOSES over it and does not build one; (c) confirm task-af9454f4's disclosure arm is still present and still asserts the defective behaviour. If any has moved, BLOCK and name the read.

NEVER WEAKEN THE VERIFICATION. The fix changes what is REFERENCED, never whether it is checked. A diff that deletes the recomputation, adds a tolerance, gates it behind a flag, or lets a caller influence the comparison fails DoD 3 and 4 regardless of what the suite says. Trading a false-positive tamper for a silent one is worse than the defect.

DO NOT WIDEN SCOPE INTO THE HANDOFF CONTRACT ITSELF. task-af9454f4 disclosed separately that RELEASED is unreachable in production (`noteRelease` passes `handoff: null`) and that a server-side nine-key builder would retire the scheduler handoff relay. Those are lane-level items with their own owner. This row fixes the referent of an existing binding and nothing else.

SHARED WORKTREE. Peers are live in apps/daemon/src. Edit files in place; never regenerate or restore a shared file from an earlier copy — that is a whole-file write and it destroys uncommitted peer work silently. After writing any shared file run `git diff --stat <path>` and compare the insertion count to your own edit; smaller than your own edit means you overwrote someone. If you must stage without touching the worktree copy, use index-only surgery (`git show HEAD:<path> | <edit> | git hash-object -w --stdin` then `git update-index --cacheinfo`) and finish with a BARE `git commit` — never `-a`, never a pathspec, both of which read the worktree.

DRILL RESTORE PROOF: `git diff` is blind to untracked paths. Before drilling, `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths; for any untracked one, prove the restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Re-run every arm after applying its migration, and re-run the PREDICTED reds first — an arm that reddens for the reason you expected is where a second cause hides.
